questions.qtext: Which of the following is not true with respect to deadlock prevention and deadlock avoidance schemes?

options.text: In deadlock prevention, the request for resources is always granted if resulting state is safe.
In deadlock avoidance, the request for resources is always granted, if the resulting state is safe.
Deadlock avoidance requires knowledge of resource requirements a priori.
Deadlock prevention is more restrictive than deadlock avoidance.

questions.solution:
(a)
Deadlock prevention can be done by eliminating any of below condition.
(i) Mutual exclusion
(ii) Hold and wait
(iii) No preemption
(iv) Circular wait
In deadlock prevention, the request for resource is not always granted if the resulting state is safe.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statement are correct?

options.text: Contiguous allocation is suffer from external fragmentation.

questions.solution:

(b) False: Linked allocation is no external fragmentation.

options.text: Demand paging brings a page into the memory only then it is needed.
Demand paging requires more main memory than normal paging.
Demand paging can bring entire process into memory at load time (for very small processes).
In demand paging, a given instruction can lead to page fault.

questions.solution:
(a, c, d)
(a) Lazy swapper concept is implemented in demand paging in which a page is not swapped into memory unless it is required.
(b) Process larger than the main memory can be executed because of demand paging.
(c) More processes may be maintained in the main memory.
(d) The process of loading the page into memory on demand (whenever page fault occurs) is known as demand paging.
